(as ''NK Bežigrad'') | chrtitle = President | chairman = Adam Delius | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = Jugoslav Trenchovski | league = [[Slovenian PrvaLiga]] | position = Slovenian PrvaLiga, 4th of 10 | season = [[2025–26 Slovenian PrvaLiga|2025–26]] | current = | website = {{URL|https://nkolimpija.si}} | pattern_la1 = _olimpija2627h | pattern_b1 = _olimpija2627h | pattern_ra1 = _olimpija2627h | pattern_sh1 = _olimpija2627h | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = | body1 = | rightarm1 = | shorts1 = | socks1 = 00853e | pattern_la2 = _olimpija2526a | pattern_b2 = _olimpija2526a | pattern_ra2 = _olimpija2526a | pattern_sh2 = _olimpija2526a | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = | socks2 = 000000 | pattern_la3 = _olimpija2526t | pattern_b3 = _olimpija2526t | pattern_ra3 = _olimpija2526t | pattern_sh3 = _olimpija2526t | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = 0D7E73 }} {{Olimpija Ljubljana sections}} '''Nogometni klub Olimpija Ljubljana''' ({{IPA|sl|nɔɡɔˈméːtni ˈklúːp ɔˈlìːmpija ljubˈljàːna}}; {{langx|en|Olimpija Ljubljana Football Club}}), commonly referred to as '''Olimpija Ljubljana''' or simply '''Olimpija''', is a Slovenian professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Ljubljana]] that competes in the [[Slovenian PrvaLiga]], the top division of the [[Football in Slovenia#League system|Slovenian football league system]]. They have won four Slovenian PrvaLiga titles and four [[Slovenian Football Cup|Slovenian Cups]]. Founded on 2 March 2005 as ''NK Bežigrad'', Olimpija began competing in the Slovenian fifth division during the 2005–06 season and managed to achieve promotion in four successive seasons, reaching the top division for the first time in 2009 after winning the [[2008–09 Slovenian Second League]]. After seven years in the top division, Olimpija won their first major trophy when they were crowned champions in the [[2015–16 Slovenian PrvaLiga|2015–16]] season. They won three more league titles in [[2017–18 Slovenian PrvaLiga|2017–18]], [[2022–23 Slovenian PrvaLiga|2022–23]] and [[2024–25 Slovenian PrvaLiga|2024–25]]; in 2017–18, Olimpija also won the [[2017–18 Slovenian Football Cup|national cup]] for the first time, completing their first [[Double (association football)|double]]. Initially, the club played at the [[Bežigrad Stadium]] and the [[ŽŠD Ljubljana Stadium|ŽAK Stadium]] during the club's stay in the second division and during the first year in the top division. In 2010, they moved to the [[Stožice Stadium]] with a capacity of 16,038. Olimpija's nicknames are the "Green and Whites" (''{{langx|sl|Zeleno-beli}}''), referring to their primary colours, and "The Dragons" (''{{langx|sl|Zmaji}}''), referring to the dragon which is a symbol of Ljubljana and is represented on the city's [[coat of arms]] and on the club's crest. Their main rivals are [[NK Maribor]], with whom they contest the [[Eternal derby of Slovenian football (2007)|Eternal derby]]."}}
